primary_topics: Necrological speech for Dr. Jovito R. Salonga, CJP's guru and surrogate father, delivered March 14, 2016

Finding the guru: the 1956-57 FEU law student strike -- new Dean Salonga single-handedly faced 1,000 hostile students and in 30 minutes sent them back to their classrooms, 'convinced of the wisdom, honesty and sincerity of their new dean'

Finding the surrogate father: Salonga's consolation after the Yale travel grant denial ('Come join my law office and I will teach you what I learned from UP, Harvard and Yale'); three years of apprenticeship; life-defining values of integrity, prudence and fairness

Salonga's one great teaching: the distinction between things money can buy (food, clothing, shelter, sports, recreation) and things money cannot buy (excellence, integrity, honor, dignity, reverential love for God) -- CJP's governing life philosophy
sub_topics: Salonga's public profile: 'unpretentious scholar, assiduous bar topnotcher, prolific book writer, persuasive preacher, noted law dean, congressmen's congressman, three times senatorial election topnotcher, revered Senate president, dedicated human rights advocate, passionate political reformer, patriot par excellence and quintessential statesman'

The 1956-57 FEU strike: 1,000 law students protested what they perceived was the unjustified retirement of Dean Francisco Lavides; new 36-year-old Dean Salonga faced the hostile crowd with a 'forceful tremolo'; in 30 minutes sent everyone back to their classrooms
Salonga's constant reminder to CJP: as an activist student (FEU CSO President; NUSP founder), Salonga 'constantly reminded me that my first duty was to excel in academics'
Bar exams 1960: got sick; wanted to quit; Salonga 'would not hear of it'; with his encouragement CJP placed 6th
Yale scholarship denied: granted by Yale Law School; US Embassy denied travel grant; Salonga's consolation and law office invitation

Three-year apprenticeship: 'taught me the rudiments of law practice and, more important, the life-defining values of integrity, prudence and fairness. He led by example, not by words. He was a dedicated husband, a caring father, a faithful friend and a devoted man of God. He did not smoke, drink or gamble. He lived almost an ascetic life.'

Different faiths, same bond: Salonga was a devout Protestant; CJP a fledgling Catholic; 'we never discussed what separated us, only what truly bound us' -- over 50 years of surrogate father-son relationship

Greatest honor: Salonga retained CJP as his personal legal counsel when Senate president and chief legal counsel of the Liberal Party -- 'Nothing is more fulfilling, more exhilarating than the honor of being counsel to one's guru and former boss!'

Dissolving the law firm: before joining Cory Aquino's Cabinet in 1986, Salonga dissolved his law firm 'not because this was mandated by law but because of his strict, self-imposed, personal ethic of being beyond suspicion'; CJP followed his example when joining the SC

JBC screenings: 'Several times, I failed the screening at the Judicial and Bar Council. In all those trying years, Dr. Salonga constantly cheered me up and tirelessly uplifted my sagging spirit.' Reminded CJP of Romans 8:28
A Test of Courage (2007): Salonga and Evelyn Miranda-Feliciano published a tribute book to the Panganiban Court's noble justices upon CJP's retirement

Salonga's one great teaching: 'While it is desirable to have the many necessities that money can buy... never ever forget that it is far more important to aspire for, imbibe and live by the values that money cannot buy, like excellence, integrity, honor, dignity, and a reverential regard and love for God as the Source of all that is true, good and beautiful'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered March 14, 2016 as the necrological speech for Dr. Jovito R. Salonga -- 'unpretentious scholar, assiduous bar topnotcher, prolific book writer, persuasive preacher, noted law dean, congressmen's congressman, three-times senatorial topnotcher, Senate president, human rights advocate, patriot par excellence and quintessential statesman' -- this eulogy by CJP adds the personal dimension: finding the guru and finding the surrogate father. The guru was discovered at the 1956-57 FEU student strike: 1,000 hostile law students had gone on strike over the retirement of Dean Lavides; new 36-year-old Dean Salonga faced them alone, spoke with a 'forceful tremolo,' and in 30 minutes sent them all back, 'convinced of the wisdom, honesty and sincerity of their new dean.' As a student activist, Salonga constantly reminded CJP that his first duty was to excel academically; when CJP wanted to quit the 1960 bar exams (sick, flooded exam venue), Salonga 'would not hear of it'; CJP placed 6th. The surrogate father emerged after the Yale travel grant denial: 'Come, join my law office and I will teach you what I learned from UP, Harvard and Yale' -- three years of apprenticeship producing integrity, prudence and fairness; 'He led by example, not by words. He lived almost an ascetic life... He lived simply so others may simply live.' Across different faiths (Salonga Protestant; CJP Catholic): 'we never discussed what separated us, only what truly bound us.' The greatest honor: Salonga retained CJP as his personal legal counsel as Senate president and Liberal Party chief. On dissolving the law firm before joining Cory Aquino's Cabinet: 'not because this was mandated by law but because of his strict, self-imposed, personal ethic of being beyond suspicion' -- CJP followed the same example when joining the SC. During multiple JBC rejections, Salonga 'patiently reminded me of Romans 8:28: God makes all things work together for the good of those who love Him.' After CJP's retirement, Salonga co-published 'A Test of Courage' (2007) as a tribute to the Panganiban Court. The one teaching CJP will always treasure: 'While it is desirable to have the many necessities that money can buy... never ever forget that it is far more important to aspire for, imbibe and live by the values that money cannot buy, like excellence, integrity, honor, dignity, and a reverential regard and love for God as the Source of all that is true, good and beautiful.'
